items.title: Introduction to Accounting — What You Need to Know Before Reading Financial Statements
items.description: The definition and purpose of accounting, financial accounting vs. management accounting, the double-entry bookkeeping principle, and the fundamental assumptions and qualitative characteristics of accounting — the first lecture in the Accounting Basics series.

items.title: Financial Ratio Analysis — Diagnosing a Company's Health Through Numbers
items.description: Profitability, liquidity, solvency, activity, growth, and valuation ratio analysis, DuPont analysis, and industry-based ratio benchmarking — the tenth and final lecture in the Accounting Basics series.

items.title: Working Capital & Turnover Ratios — Reading Liquidity and Cash Conversion Speed
items.description: Current ratio, quick ratio, accounts receivable turnover, and inventory turnover — how to use these four metrics to assess a company's short-term payment capacity and cash conversion speed. Eleventh lecture in the Accounting Basics series.

items.title: Cost Budgets and Variance Analysis Explained
items.description: Fixed versus flexible budgets, and how price, volume and efficiency variances reveal where cost control actually broke down.

items.title: The Balance Sheet — How to Read a Company Through Assets, Liabilities, and Equity
items.description: The structure and account classifications of the balance sheet, current and non-current assets, current and non-current liabilities, and the components of equity — the second lecture in the Accounting Basics series.

items.title: The Income Statement — How to Read Business Performance Through Revenue and Expenses
items.description: The structure of the income statement, principles of revenue and expense recognition, calculating gross profit, operating income, and net income, and accrual vs. cash-basis accounting — the third lecture in the Accounting Basics series.

items.title: The Cash Flow Statement — Why Profit and Cash Are Not the Same Thing
items.description: The three-section structure of the cash flow statement (operating, investing, and financing activities), the direct and indirect methods, free cash flow (FCF), and the difference between profit and cash — the fourth lecture in the Accounting Basics series.

items.title: Property, Plant & Equipment and Depreciation — From Acquisition to Disposal
items.description: Determining the cost of PP&E, depreciation methods (straight-line, declining balance, units of production), capital expenditures vs. revenue expenditures, and asset impairment — the fifth lecture in the Accounting Basics series.

items.title: Inventory and Cost Accounting — CVP Analysis and the Fundamentals of Cost Calculation
items.description: Inventory valuation methods (FIFO and weighted average), the components of manufacturing cost, and CVP (cost-volume-profit) analysis including break-even point calculation — the sixth lecture in the Accounting Basics series.

items.title: Tax Accounting Fundamentals — Corporate Income Tax and Tax Adjustments
items.description: The structure of corporate income tax, the differences between financial accounting and tax accounting, tax adjustments (add-backs and deductions), and deferred taxes — the seventh lecture in the Accounting Basics series.

items.title: Auditing — Can You Trust the Financial Statements?
items.description: The purpose and procedures of a financial statement audit, types of audit opinions (unqualified, qualified, adverse, disclaimer), internal controls, and the audit risk model — the eighth lecture in the Accounting Basics series.

items.title: IFRS and Global Accounting Standards — Understanding the Global Language of Finance
items.description: The background of IFRS adoption, key differences from US GAAP, fair value accounting, consolidated financial statements, and major IFRS standards — the ninth lecture in the Accounting Basics series.

items.description: Definition and history of AI, narrow vs. general AI, the AI winters, and real-world applications.

items.description: Supervised, unsupervised and reinforcement learning — key algorithms, overfitting versus underfitting, and the bias-variance tradeoff.

items.description: Artificial neural network architecture, activation functions, backpropagation, CNN vs. RNN vs. Transformer.

items.title: NLP and LLMs: How Transformers Actually Work
items.description: Tokenization, embeddings and attention explained, plus how BERT and GPT differ and what that means for prompt engineering.

items.title: Computer Vision — How Computers See the World

items.title: Model Evaluation and Optimization — What Makes a Good AI Model?
items.description: Accuracy alone isn't enough. Precision, recall, F1, ROC-AUC, cross-validation, hyperparameter tuning — the evaluation toolkit of real ML practice.

items.title: Generative AI — GANs, Diffusion Models, and How ChatGPT Works
items.description: AI that creates images, writes text, and composes music. From GANs to diffusion models to GPT-4 — the core principles of generative AI.

items.title: AI Ethics and the Future — Principles for Responsible AI
items.description: As AI grows more powerful, ethical questions grow weightier. Bias, privacy, explainability, AGI risk — the ethics knowledge essential for the AI era.

items.title: AI in Practice — Reading Financial Statements with AI: An Accounting Primer for Non-Specialists
items.description: Learn to analyze the income statement, balance sheet, and cash flow statement with AI, and pick up practical techniques for quickly gauging a company's financial health.

items.title: AI in Practice — Using AI to Analyze Job Postings and Write Your Cover Letter
items.description: A step-by-step guide to analyzing job postings and drafting a tailored cover letter with ChatGPT or Claude — an AI strategy for boosting your chances of getting hired.

items.description: How to write business emails, meeting minutes, and Slack messages efficiently with ChatGPT or Claude — an AI strategy for more effective communication.

items.description: ALB, NLB, GLB comparison, Auto Scaling Groups, scaling policies, health checks — implementing elastic architectures. AWS SAA.

items.description: CloudFront CDN, Route 53 routing policies, and cost optimization strategies — the final SAA exam topics. AWS SAA.

items.title: Behavioral Economics — Where the Standard Model Goes Wrong
items.description: Maps the whole course: which assumptions of the standard economic model behavioral economics revises (preferences, beliefs, decision processes), bounded rationality, the role of laboratory and field evidence, and the replication problem.

items.title: Behavioral Economics — Replicability, Behavioral Welfare Economics and the Limits of Policy
items.description: Closes the course by separating findings weakened by large-scale replications (such as ego depletion) from robust ones, asking what standard to use when choice and welfare diverge (behavioral welfare economics), and covering corrective taxes on internalities and firms' exploitation of biases.

items.title: Behavioral Economics — Prospect Theory I: Reference Points and Loss Aversion
items.description: Sets out with formulas and a graph the value function of prospect theory, in which utility depends on gains and losses relative to a reference point rather than on levels of wealth, and uses numerical examples to explain the loss aversion coefficient, the reflection effect and framing effects.

items.title: Behavioral Economics — Prospect Theory II: Probability Weighting and the Endowment Effect
items.description: Uses prospect theory to explain the probability weighting function that overweights small and underweights large probabilities, the Allais paradox, the fourfold pattern of risk attitudes, and the endowment effect and status quo bias, and assesses the strength of the evidence.

items.title: Behavioral Economics — Present Bias and Time Inconsistency
items.description: Shows with numbers the difference between exponential and quasi-hyperbolic (β-δ) discounting and why preference reversals occur, and covers the difference between naive and sophisticated agents, commitment devices and designs such as Save More Tomorrow.

items.title: Behavioral Economics — Judgement Heuristics and Biased Beliefs
items.description: Uses numerical examples to show how the representativeness, availability and anchoring-and-adjustment heuristics depart systematically from Bayesian updating, covering base-rate neglect, the conjunction fallacy, the gambler's fallacy, overconfidence and confirmation bias.

items.title: Behavioral Economics — Mental Accounting and Sunk Costs
items.description: Links to prospect theory, with numerical examples, mental accounting that breaks the standard assumption that money is fungible, transaction utility and reference prices, segregating and integrating gains and losses, the sunk cost effect and income-targeting behaviour.

items.title: Behavioral Economics — Social Preferences: Fairness, Reciprocity and Trust
items.description: Summarizes experimental results from the ultimatum, dictator, public goods and trust games, computes rejection thresholds with the Fehr-Schmidt inequity aversion model, and covers reciprocity, gift exchange and the crowding out of motivation by monetary incentives.

items.title: Behavioral Economics — Behavioral Finance: Limits to Arbitrage and Investor Biases
items.description: Covers why arbitrage cannot correct prices even when biased investors are present (limits to arbitrage), field evidence on the disposition effect and excessive trading, and the equity premium puzzle seen through myopic loss aversion.

items.title: Behavioral Economics — Choice Architecture and Nudges
items.description: Covers evidence that defaults, social norms and the presentation of information change choices (automatic pension enrolment, energy reports), large-scale tests of the size of nudge effects, and libertarian paternalism and its critics.

items.title: Big Data Fundamentals — The 5Vs, Hadoop, and the Data Pipeline

items.description: Descriptive statistics, distributions, missing value treatment, outlier detection, normalization and encoding — the essential steps before modeling.

items.title: Statistics for Data Science — Hypothesis Testing and Distributions
items.description: Probability distributions, hypothesis testing (t-test/chi-square/ANOVA), p-values, Type I/II errors — the statistical foundation of data analytics.

items.title: Classification Algorithms — Logistic Regression to Random Forest
items.description: Logistic regression, decision trees, random forests, SVM, naive Bayes — comparing classification algorithms.

items.title: Regression Analysis and Time Series Forecasting
items.description: Linear regression, Ridge/Lasso regularization, time series decomposition, ARIMA — predicting numerical outcomes.

items.title: Clustering and Unsupervised Learning
items.description: K-means, hierarchical clustering, DBSCAN, PCA dimensionality reduction — finding patterns in unlabeled data.

items.title: Data Visualization and Interpreting Results
items.description: Choosing the right chart, histograms, box plots, scatter plots, heatmaps, and dashboard design principles.

items.description: TF-IDF, morphological analysis, sentiment analysis, LDA topic modeling, Apache Spark — the final chapter of Big Data Analytics.

items.title: Buddhism in Modern Terms — The Buddha's Teaching: Reading the Four Noble Truths and the Eightfold Path for Today

items.title: Buddhism in Modern Terms — Wonhyo's Philosophy of Hwajaeng: A One-Mind Philosophy That Holds Contradiction
items.description: The philosophy of Hwajaeng, developed by the Silla-era monk Wonhyo, rendered into modern language. Applying to daily life one of Korean Buddhism's greatest philosophical insights — reconciling 'difference' into oneness without denying it.

items.title: Buddhism in Modern Terms — Hwaeom Thought: Indra's Net and a World Where One Is All
items.description: Indra's net and the principle that 'the one is the many, the many is the one,' rendered into modern language. Understanding Hwaeom's insight — a world where everything is interconnected — alongside ecology and network thinking.

items.title: Buddhism in Modern Terms — The Lotus Sūtra: Every Being's Potential for Buddhahood and the Bodhisattva Path
items.description: The Lotus Sūtra's core teaching — the One Vehicle and the potential of every being to attain Buddhahood — rendered into modern language. Exploring what the bodhisattva way of life means for us today.

items.title: International Economics (Trade & Finance)
items.description: Study the principles of international trade through comparative advantage and exchange rate determination mechanisms, and summarize macroeconomic policies in an open economy.

items.title: Macroeconomics — The Consumption Function: From Keynes to Permanent Income
items.description: Computes the multiplier with the Keynesian consumption function and Keynesian cross, and then, starting from the Kuznets puzzle, covers the permanent-income and life-cycle hypotheses, random-walk consumption and why liquidity constraints change the marginal propensity to consume, with numbers and a graph.

items.title: Macroeconomics — The Investment Function: The User Cost of Capital
items.description: Explains with numbers and a graph how firms set a target capital stock by comparing the marginal product of capital with the user cost (r+δ)P_k, how interest-rate changes feed into investment, the accelerator, Tobin's q, and why irreversibility and credit constraints make investment insensitive to interest rates.

items.title: Macroeconomics — Applying IS-LM: Slopes and Schools of Thought
items.description: Derives fiscal and monetary multipliers from IS-LM parameters, computes with the same numbers and a graph how the effects of both policies change as the interest sensitivity of money demand ranges from infinity (liquidity trap) to zero (classical case), and discusses the policy mix.

items.title: Macroeconomics — AD-AS and the Price Level
items.description: Derives the aggregate demand curve by letting the price level vary in IS-LM, then combines the upward-sloping short-run aggregate supply created by price stickiness with the vertical long-run aggregate supply to compute, with the same numbers and a graph, the short- and long-run effects of a monetary expansion and of supply shocks.

items.title: Microeconomics — Supply, Demand and Comparative Statics
items.description: Solves the linear supply-and-demand equilibrium in general form, shows how the signs of price and quantity changes identify which curve moved, and computes the shortage and deadweight loss of a price ceiling, with numbers and a graph.

items.title: Macroeconomics — Expectations: From Adaptive to Rational
items.description: Uses the expectations-augmented Phillips curve to show the short-run trade-off and the vertical long run on a graph, computes accelerating inflation under adaptive expectations and the sacrifice ratio of disinflation, and covers rational expectations, policy ineffectiveness, credibility and anchored expectations.

items.title: Macroeconomics — Business Cycles: Demand Shocks and Supply Shocks
items.description: Covers the stylized facts of business cycles (comovement, volatile investment), how to tell demand shocks from supply shocks by the signs of output and prices, the policy dilemma of stagflation, the difference between real business cycle theory and New Keynesian economics, and how shocks propagate.

items.title: Macroeconomics — The Solow Growth Model
items.description: Finds the steady state from the dynamics of capital per worker, sf(k) = (δ+n)k, and uses numbers and graphs to explain why the saving rate changes the level of output but not the long-run growth rate, the Golden Rule capital stock and consumption during the transition, conditional convergence and the role of technological progress.

items.title: Macroeconomics — Endogenous Growth and the Solow Residual
items.description: Computes the Solow residual with growth accounting, explains why the saving rate changes the growth rate in the AK model where diminishing returns to capital disappear, and covers the non-rivalry of ideas and the undersupply of R&D, human capital, the critique of scale effects and the role of institutions.

items.title: Macroeconomics — The Trade-offs of Stabilization Policy
items.description: Covers Tinbergen's targets-and-instruments principle, uses a central bank loss function to compute how the optimal response to a supply shock splits it between inflation and the output gap, and explains the Taylor rule, rules versus discretion and time inconsistency, policy lags and financial stability.

items.title: Macroeconomics — Effective Demand and When the Multiplier Works
items.description: Computes with numbers how gaps between planned spending and actual output adjust output through inventories, how the multiplier builds up round by round, how much leakages (taxes and imports) shrink it and the paradox of thrift, and sets out the conditions under which the multiplier works.

items.title: Economics Basics — Macroeconomics, Money and National Economy
items.description: Complete summary of Keynes' effective demand theory, aggregate demand-aggregate supply (AD-AS) model, money market and interest rate determination, monetary policy spillover path, and bank's credit...

items.title: Macroeconomics — Short-Run and Long-Run Adjustment in AD-AS
items.description: Computes year by year the path back to long-run equilibrium as expected prices and wages catch up after a demand shock, and covers what sets the speed of adjustment, downward nominal wage rigidity, debt deflation, hysteresis and the difference between temporary and permanent supply shocks.

items.title: Macroeconomics — Money Demand and the Interest Rate
items.description: Uses numbers to cover Keynes's three motives for holding money, the square-root formula for transactions money demand derived from the Baumol-Tobin inventory model, velocity and the stability of money demand, how payment technology shifts the LM curve, and the inflation tax.

items.title: Macroeconomics — Fiscal and Monetary Multipliers and Crowding Out
items.description: Uses IS-LM numbers to compare how much the same fiscal expansion raises output depending on the central bank's response (fixed money, fixed rate, tightening), and covers exchange-rate crowding out in an open economy, Ricardian equivalence and the risk of fiscal dominance.

items.title: Macroeconomics — Bank Credit and the Central Bank Balance Sheet
items.description: Follows the central bank and commercial bank balance sheets to see how the monetary base and deposits are created, and uses numbers to cover the modern view that loans create deposits, how quantitative easing works, and where bank capital ratios and the credit channel block monetary transmission.

items.title: Microeconomics — Elasticity and Tax Incidence
items.description: Covers point and arc elasticity and their link to revenue (MR = P(1−1/|ε|)), why elasticity changes along a linear demand curve, income and cross elasticities, and how a tax burden is split according to relative elasticities, with numbers and a graph.

items.title: Macroeconomics — Disputes Between Schools Are Bundles of Assumptions
items.description: Organizes the classical, Keynesian, monetarist, new classical, real business cycle and New Keynesian schools as combinations of assumptions about price flexibility, expectations and policy rules, and covers the conditions for policy ineffectiveness, evidence on monetary shocks and changes since the financial crisis.

items.title: Economics Basics — Economic Stability Policy Debate and Inflation
items.description: Intensive analysis of genealogy from classical school to new Keynesian school, Phillips curve, crowding-out effect debate, types of unemployment, and ripple effects of inflation

items.title: Macroeconomics — Unemployment as Stocks and Flows
items.description: Computes how the number of unemployed (a stock) is set by separations and job finding (flows) with the steady-state rate s/(s+f), uses the Beveridge curve to distinguish deficient demand from worse matching, and covers how unemployment benefits, employment protection and efficiency wages change the flows.

items.title: Macroeconomics — The Costs of Inflation, Expected and Unexpected
items.description: Uses numbers to separate the costs of expected inflation (shoe-leather, menu costs, unindexed taxes) from the redistribution caused by unexpected inflation, and covers inflation variability and relative-price distortion, the dangers of hyperinflation and deflation, and why inflation targets are 2%.

items.title: Macroeconomics — Comparing Growth Models
items.description: Tabulates where the Solow, human-capital-augmented Solow, AK and idea-based models make different predictions about saving and R&D, and covers the speed of convergence, development accounting, the East Asian growth debate and criteria for judging growth policy.

items.title: Economics Basics — Economic Growth and International Economy
items.description: Solow model, endogenous growth, basic import/export trade strategy, advantages and disadvantages of fixed/floating exchange rates, and structure of the global financial crisis.

items.title: Macroeconomics — Solving IS-LM Simultaneously and Comparative Statics
items.description: Solves linear IS-LM as a system of equations (matrices and Cramer's rule) to get general solutions for equilibrium output and the interest rate, checks the comparative-static coefficients for government spending and real balances against earlier chapters' numbers, and shows where the interest-rate lower bound breaks the linear solution.

items.title: Microeconomics — Consumer Theory: Utility Maximisation and Choice
items.description: Derives the optimality condition MRS = Px/Py from the budget constraint and indifference curves with a Lagrangian, and covers Cobb–Douglas demand, corner solutions and the Slutsky decomposition into substitution and income effects, with numbers and a graph.

items.title: Economics — Comparative Advantage — Why Trade Benefits Everyone
items.description: Learn the gains from trade through David Ricardo's theory of comparative advantage — how countries benefit by specializing in what they produce at the lowest opportunity cost. Analyze it yourself with the interactive opportunity cost calculator.

items.title: Microeconomics — Game Theory: Mixed Strategies, Repetition and Credibility
items.description: Finds mixed-strategy Nash equilibria from indifference conditions when no pure-strategy equilibrium exists, and covers backward induction and subgame-perfect equilibrium in an entry game, non-credible threats and commitment, and the critical discount factor of repeated games, with numerical examples.

items.title: Microeconomics — Producer Theory: Cost Minimisation and Profit
items.description: Derives the cost-minimisation condition MRTS = w/r from the production function and isoquants, explains the relationship among short-run cost curves (MC, AVC, ATC) and the shutdown condition P < AVC, and covers returns to scale and long-run average cost, with numbers and a graph.

items.title: Microeconomics — Perfect Competition: Short-Run Supply and Zero Long-Run Profit
items.description: Builds industry supply from individual firms' supply curves, follows with numbers and a graph how entry and exit push price to minimum average cost in the long run, and covers constant-, increasing- and decreasing-cost industries and why competition is efficient.

items.title: Microeconomics — Monopoly: Quantity, Price and Deadweight Loss
items.description: Explains why a monopolist's marginal revenue lies below price, computes the MR = MC output and the deadweight loss, the Lerner index and the inverse-elasticity pricing rule, third-degree price discrimination, and the options for regulating a natural monopoly, with numbers and a graph.

items.title: Microeconomics — Oligopoly and Monopolistic Competition
items.description: Compares, on a single demand curve with numbers and a graph, Cournot reaction functions and Nash equilibrium, the Stackelberg leader's advantage, the Bertrand paradox, the incentive to cheat on a cartel and the critical discount factor in a repeated game, and the long-run excess capacity of monopolistic competition.

items.title: Microeconomics — Factor Markets and Distribution
items.description: Shows that labour demand is a derived demand based on the value of the marginal product, explains how output-market monopoly and monopsony reduce employment, when a minimum wage can raise employment under monopsony, and covers wage differentials and economic rent, with numbers and a graph.

items.title: Mathematics for Economics — Functions, Derivatives, and Economic Applications
items.description: Mathematics for economics — function basics, marginal vs. average concepts, basic differentiation rules (product, quotient, chain), elasticity in economics, profit optimization, and cost function analysis, in one complete guide.

items.title: Mathematics for Economics — Integrals, Matrices, and Economic Applications
items.description: Mathematics for economics — indefinite and definite integrals with economic applications (consumer and producer surplus), matrix operations and inverse matrices, systems of equations (input-output analysis), and the basics of difference and differential equations, in one complete guide.

items.title: Mathematics for Economics — Game Theory and Optimization
items.description: Mathematics for economics — game theory basics (normal-form games, Nash equilibrium, the prisoner's dilemma), repeated games and cooperation, multivariable optimization (the Lagrange multiplier method), the basics of linear programming, and auction theory, in one complete guide.

items.title: Mathematics for Economics — Dynamic Optimization, Behavioral Economics Math, and Networks
items.description: Mathematics for economics — dynamic optimization (the Euler equation, the Bellman equation, continuous-time optimization), stochastic processes (Markov chains, Brownian motion, option pricing), the mathematical foundations of behavioral economics, and network economics, in one complete guide.

items.title: Parts of Speech: Nouns and Pronouns
items.description: Learn the foundation of English grammar by mastering nouns and pronouns, including countable, uncountable, and pronoun types.

items.title: Gerunds and Infinitives: -ing vs To
items.description: Learn which verbs take gerunds, which take infinitives, and which take both — including the crucial meaning differences that change everything.

items.title: Modal Verbs: Ability, Permission, Obligation, and Possibility
items.description: A complete guide to English modal verbs — can, could, may, might, must, should, will, would, and shall — with usage tables and examples.

items.title: Reported Speech: Telling What Others Said
items.description: Learn how to convert direct speech to reported speech in English, including tense backshift, pronoun changes, and time expression adjustments.

items.title: Relative Clauses: who, which, that, where, when
items.description: Master English relative clauses — defining vs non-defining, relative pronouns, and how to reduce clauses for more concise writing.

items.title: Top 10 Grammar Errors and How to Fix Them
items.description: Identify and correct the 10 most common English grammar mistakes — from its/it's confusion to dangling modifiers — with clear correction examples.

items.title: Advanced Grammar: Cohesion, Coherence, and Style
items.description: Elevate your English writing with advanced grammar tools — discourse markers, parallel structure, sentence variety, and academic hedging language.

items.title: Mastering Verb Tenses
items.description: A comprehensive guide to all 12 English verb tenses, with timelines, usage rules, and the most common errors learners make.

items.title: Adjectives and Adverbs: Describing the World
items.description: Master adjectives and adverbs — their comparative and superlative forms, placement rules, and the most common mistakes learners make.

items.title: Building Sentences: From Simple to Complex
items.description: Understand the three types of English sentences — simple, compound, and complex — and learn to build them with the right conjunctions.

items.title: The Article System: A, An, and The
items.description: Master English articles — definite, indefinite, and zero article — with clear rules, a decision table, and fixes for the most common non-native errors.

items.title: Prepositions of Time, Place, and Direction
items.description: Conquer English prepositions of time, place, and direction with clear rules, collocation tables, and common error corrections.

items.title: Forming Questions and Negative Sentences
items.description: Learn how to form yes/no questions, Wh-questions, and negatives in English using auxiliary verbs do, does, and did.

items.title: The Passive Voice: When the Object Becomes Subject
items.description: Understand how to form and use the passive voice in English, including tense changes, when to use it, and common mistakes to avoid.

items.title: If Clauses: Zero, First, Second, and Third Conditionals
items.description: Master all four English conditional sentence types — zero, first, second, and third — with a clear structure table and common error fixes.

items.title: Alchemy of Wealth: Goals of Finance and Time Value of Money
items.description: Understand the ultimate goal of financial management—maximizing corporate value—and master the concept of Time Value of Money (TVM), the bedrock of all financial decision-making.

items.title: Finance Without Borders: International Finance
items.description: Understand the mechanics of the global financial system. Learn about Exchange Rate determination, Purchasing Power Parity (PPP), and how to manage the risks and opportunities of doing business acro...

items.title: Finance — Capital Budgeting and NPV — Capturing Future Value in the Present
items.description: Master NPV (Net Present Value), the core tool of capital budgeting for long-term corporate investment decisions. Explore the relationship between discount rates and cash flows using the interactive NPV calculator.

items.title: Finance — Cost of Capital and CAPM — Pricing the Risk
items.description: Understand the true nature of cost of capital — the minimum return investors require for committing funds to a business. Master the Capital Asset Pricing Model (CAPM) and Weighted Average Cost of Capital (WACC) with interactive calculators.

items.title: Finance — Bond Valuation — The Elegance of Fixed Income
items.description: How is a bond's price determined when its future cash flows are already promised? Explore the inverse relationship between coupon rate and market interest rate with an interactive bond calculator.

items.title: Finance — Portfolio Theory and Diversification — Don't Put All Your Eggs in One Basket
items.description: Master Harry Markowitz's Modern Portfolio Theory (MPT) — how combining assets with low correlation reduces risk without sacrificing returns. Includes a visualization tool to bring the concepts to life.

items.title: Aesthetics of Price and Value: Valuation of Stocks and Bonds
items.description: Understand how the intrinsic value of financial assets is determined, and master sophisticated valuation methods through Yield to Maturity (YTM) for bonds and the Dividend Discount Model (DDM) for ...

items.title: Don't Put All Your Eggs in One Basket: Risk, Return, and Portfolio Theory
items.description: Master the statistical foundations of measuring risk and return, and discover the magic of the 'Portfolio Effect'—reducing risk through diversification.

items.title: Pricing the Risk: Capital Asset Pricing Model (CAPM) and Beta
items.description: Understand the CAPM, the definitive model of modern finance that explains the relationship between systematic risk and return. Explore 'Beta' as a measure of market sensitivity and learn to value a...

items.title: The Moment of Decision: Capital Budgeting (NPV vs. IRR)
items.description: Learn how companies decide on major investments. Master the Net Present Value (NPV) and Internal Rate of Return (IRR) methods to evaluate the feasibility of business projects.

items.title: The Cost of Money: Weighted Average Cost of Capital (WACC)
items.description: Analyze the 'Opportunity Cost' that companies pay to raise capital. Master how to mix Equity and Debt to find WACC, the ultimate hurdle rate for business decisions.

items.title: The Art of Leverage: Capital Structure and Enterprise Value
items.description: Explore how the mix of Debt and Equity affects a company's value and risk. Understand the Modigliani-Miller (MM) theorems and the trade-off between tax benefits and bankruptcy costs.

items.title: Rules of the Harvest: Dividend Policy and Shareholder Return
items.description: Understand how companies decide to distribute wealth. Learn about the 'Dividend Irrelevance' theory, the signaling effect of payouts, and the strategic choice between dividends and share buybacks.

items.title: Shield and Sword: Derivatives and Risk Management
items.description: Learn how to protect business value in a volatile world. Master the concepts of Forwards, Futures, Options, and Swaps, and understand how 'Hedge' functions as a safety net for corporate finance.

items.title: The World of Financial Engineering
items.description: An introduction to the history, core concepts, and the role of 'quants' in modern finance.

items.title: Portfolio Optimization: Finding the Optimal Investment Mix
items.description: Based on Harry Markowitz's Modern Portfolio Theory (MPT), learn the principles of optimal asset allocation to maximize returns for a given risk level or minimize risk for a specific return target.

items.title: Financial Machine Learning Fundamentals: Data Moves Capital
items.description: Beyond traditional quantitative strategies, you will learn the basic concepts of machine learning, which learns non-linear patterns through massive data, and practical use cases such as algorithmic...

items.title: Limits and future of financial engineering: lessons learned from the crisis
items.description: We look back at cases where mathematical models distorted irrational madness or extreme crises in the real world, and look at the future of financial engineering that evolves along with new trends ...

items.title: The Time Value of Money: Why Interest Matters
items.description: Understand the fundamental concept of compounding and discounting, and how the value of money changes across time.

items.title: Basics of Derivatives: Forward and Futures
items.description: Learn the core concepts of derivatives and how forward contracts are used to manage price risk in an uncertain future.

items.title: Option Trading and Payoff Structures: The Magic of Asymmetric Returns
items.description: Understand the fundamental concepts of Call and Put options, and visualize the asymmetric profit/loss structures for buyers and sellers based on price movements.

items.title: The Black-Scholes Model: The Standard for Option Pricing
items.description: Understand the fundamental assumptions of the Nobel Prize-winning Black-Scholes model and mathematically analyze how stock prices, time, and volatility affect option prices.

items.title: The Greeks: The Language of Risk
items.description: Learn about the Greek letters that quantify the impact of changes in underlying asset price, time, and volatility on option prices, and understand risk hedging techniques using them.

items.title: Monte Carlo Simulation: Mapping Tens of Thousands of Futures
items.description: Learn numerical techniques that use random numbers to generate virtual scenarios and calculate the value of complex derivatives that are difficult to solve with closed-form formulas.

items.title: Risk Measurement and Management (VaR): Quantifying Worst-Case Scenarios
items.description: Learn about Value at Risk (VaR), the standard risk management metric for financial institutions, including its calculation methods and limitations.

items.title: Introduction to Interest Rate Models: Stochastic Movement of Interest Rates
items.description: Understand the principles of bond pricing and Mean Reversion through the Vasicek and CIR models, which describe how interest rates change over time.

items.title: Introduction to Food and Nutrition Science — Types and Functions of Nutrients
items.description: College food and nutrition science — the types and functions of the six essential nutrient groups, the metabolism of carbohydrates, protein, and fat, vitamins and minerals, and the role of water.

items.title: Food and Nutrition Science — Vitamins, Minerals, Hydration, and Health
items.description: Food and nutrition science — the functions and deficiency symptoms of fat-soluble and water-soluble vitamins, key minerals (calcium, iron, sodium), water metabolism, and South Korea's dietary reference intakes.

items.title: Food and Nutrition Science — Energy Metabolism and Weight Management
items.description: Food and nutrition science — units of energy and converting food to energy, basal metabolic rate (BMR), activity energy expenditure, and total energy expenditure, the principles of weight management, nutritional-status assessment (anthropometrics, biochemistry), and meal planning.

items.title: Food and Nutrition Science — Medical Nutrition Therapy and Sports Nutrition
items.description: Food and nutrition science — medical nutrition therapy for diabetes, hypertension, obesity, and kidney disease; nutritional support for cancer patients; sports nutrition (energy systems, carb loading, hydration strategy, supplements); and lifecycle nutrition across pregnancy, lactation, infancy, and old age.

items.title: Geology — Rocks, Strata, Geologic Time, and Minerals
items.description: Geology — minerals (silicates, physical properties, crystal structure), the rock cycle (igneous, sedimentary, metamorphic rock), strata (bedding, fossils, relative and absolute age), geologic time (the Precambrian, Paleozoic, Mesozoic, Cenozoic, and mass extinctions), and Korean peninsula geology.

items.title: Geology — Economic Geology, Resource Geology, and Environmental Geology
items.description: Geology — economic geology (metallic, non-metallic, and energy resources), mining and the environment (acid mine drainage, the impact of mineral extraction), hydrogeology (groundwater, aquifers, contamination), environmental geology (slope stability, land subsidence, soft ground), and geohazards.

items.title: Geology — Plate Tectonics, Geophysics, and Seismology
items.description: Geology — plate tectonics (continental drift, plate boundaries, the Wilson cycle, mountain building), geophysics (seismic waves, Earth's internal structure, the geomagnetic field), and seismology (earthquake mechanisms, magnitude, intensity, and seismic-hazard assessment).

items.title: Comparative History: Origins of Humanity & Ancient Civilizations
items.description: Understand the transition from the Stone Age to the Neolithic Revolution and the birth of the four major civilizations by comparing the timelines of East and West.

items.title: World History Wrap-Up — The Making of the Modern World and Historical Thinking
items.description: A complete review of the World History Fundamentals series. From World War II through the Cold War, decolonization, and the 21st-century world order — master the cause-and-effect thinking that unlocks historical understanding.

items.title: Age of Empires & Philosophies: Greco-Roman vs. Qin-Han
items.description: Compare the Greco-Roman world, the roots of Western democracy and law, with the Qin-Han empires, the foundation of Eastern centralized governance and Confucian order.

items.title: The Medieval World: Feudalism, Faith, and the Crusades
items.description: Explore how feudalism structured European society after Rome's fall, how the Church wielded power, and how the Crusades reshaped the medieval world.

items.title: Renaissance and Reformation: Rediscovering Humanity
items.description: Trace how Renaissance humanism recentered human dignity, and how the Reformation shattered Christian unity and reshaped European politics and culture.

items.title: The Age of Reason: Scientific Revolution and Absolute Monarchy
items.description: Discover how Copernicus, Galileo, and Newton overthrew ancient cosmology, and how absolutist monarchs like Louis XIV centralized state power in early modern Europe.

items.title: Dual Revolution: Civil Rights and Industrial Power
items.description: Examine how the American and French Revolutions established popular sovereignty, while the Industrial Revolution transformed economies, cities, and social classes forever.

items.title: Nationalism and Empire: Unification and Imperial Expansion
items.description: Trace how nationalism drove German and Italian unification and Japan's Meiji Restoration, while European powers carved up Africa and Asia in a new wave of imperialism.

items.title: The Great War: Origins, Trenches, and the New World Order
items.description: Analyze the interlocking causes of World War I, the grinding horror of trench warfare, and how the Versailles settlement planted the seeds of future catastrophe.

items.title: The Fragile Peace: Totalitarianism Between the Wars
items.description: Examine how the Great Depression, Weimar Germany's collapse, and the rise of Fascism in Italy and Germany, alongside Stalinism in the USSR, destroyed the interwar peace.

items.title: The Art of Contracts: Poison Pill Exploration and Defense
items.description: Learn the principles and types of poison pills, a powerful weapon for corporate control defense, and master scouting methods across different legal environments.

items.title: Foundations of Law — A Complete Summary of Everyday Legal Essentials
items.description: A comprehensive summary of the Law Fundamentals series. Covers core concepts in contracts, property law, obligations, corporate law, intellectual property, and consumer protection — with practical takeaways for real-life situations.

items.title: For Workers: Toxic Clauses in Employment Contracts A to Z
items.description: Uncover the risk factors in employment contracts that you must check before signing. Learn the reality of penalty clauses, non-exempt status, and non-compete agreements.

items.title: For Freelancers: A Survival Guide to Contracts
items.description: Analyze the patterns of unfair contracts that platform workers and independent professionals frequently face. We specifically cover how to escape the cycle of copyright theft and infinite revisions.

items.title: For Businesses/B2B: Strategic Alliances and Invisible Shackles
items.description: Covers the sophisticated battle of wits in inter-company transactions. In-depth analysis of ROFR, limitation of liability, and governing law, the biggest risk in international deals.

items.title: Property Law — The Fundamentals of Ownership and Real Estate Rights
items.description: Understand the legal rights that protect your assets — the structure and types of property rights (real rights). Learn the differences between ownership, usufructuary rights, and security interests, and what real estate registration means.

items.title: Obligations Law — The Structure of Debt and Contract Performance
items.description: Learn the core of obligations law, which governs every transaction in daily life. Understand the three main sources of obligations — contracts, torts, and unjust enrichment — from creation to extinction.

items.title: Corporate Law — How a Company Is Born and Governed
items.description: Understand how a company as a legal entity is created and operated. Learn the core of corporate structure — the division of authority between the board of directors and the general meeting of shareholders, and the responsibilities of the CEO.

items.title: Intellectual Property Law — The Law That Protects Ideas
items.description: A comparative overview of the four pillars of intellectual property: patents, trademarks, copyrights, and design rights. Learn what each protects, how to register, and what remedies are available in case of infringement.

items.title: Consumer Protection Law and Data Privacy Law — Legal Shields for Modern Life
items.description: Understand two laws that have become essential in the digital age. Learn consumer rights and the right to cancel online purchases, as well as the principles of personal data processing and the rights of data subjects.

items.title: History of Medicine: From Hippocrates to Evidence-Based Practice
items.description: A journey through 2,500 years of medical history, from ancient Greece to the genomic era of modern evidence-based medicine.

items.title: Medical Fundamentals Comprehensive Review — The Science of Maintaining Health and Preventing Disease
items.description: A complete review of the Medical Fundamentals series. Understand how the major organ systems interconnect, and build practical medical knowledge spanning evidence-based preventive medicine, health screening frameworks, and lifestyle medicine.

items.title: Anatomical Organization: From Cells to Organ Systems
items.description: Explore the structural hierarchy of the human body, from cells and tissues to organs and the eleven major organ systems.

items.title: Cardiovascular System: Heart, Vessels, and Blood
items.description: Understand the cardiac cycle, blood pressure regulation, atherosclerosis, and the pharmacology of common heart medications.

items.title: Respiratory System: Gas Exchange and Breathing Mechanics
items.description: Learn how the lungs exchange oxygen and carbon dioxide, interpret spirometry values, and compare COPD with asthma clinically.

items.title: The Nervous System: CNS, PNS, and the Neuron
items.description: From neuron structure to stroke management, explore how the central and peripheral nervous systems control every body function.

items.title: Endocrine System: Hormones, Feedback, and Diabetes
items.description: Master the major endocrine glands, hormone feedback loops, and the pathophysiology and management of diabetes mellitus.

items.title: Immunology: Innate Defense, Adaptive Immunity, and Vaccines
items.description: Discover how innate and adaptive immunity protect against pathogens, how vaccines work, and the mechanisms behind autoimmune disease.

items.title: Digestive System: From Mouth to Metabolism
items.description: Trace the digestive journey from ingestion to absorption, explore liver functions, and understand IBD, IBS, and peptic ulcer disease.

items.title: The Musculoskeletal System and Skin: Organs of Movement and Protection
items.description: Understand the structure of bones and joints, the mechanics of muscle contraction, and the three-layer architecture of the skin. A concise overview of the causes and prevention of major conditions including fractures, arthritis, osteoporosis, skin cancer, and atopic dermatitis.

items.title: Origins of Music: From Ancient Rituals to Medieval Chant
items.description: Explore the earliest music-making—bone flutes, Greek modal theory, and the rise of Gregorian chant and neume notation.

items.title: Jazz Evolves: From Swing to Bebop
items.description: Follow jazz from Louis Armstrong's Hot Five recordings through big band swing to the bebop revolution of Charlie Parker and Dizzy Gillespie.

items.title: Rock Revolution: From Elvis to the Beatles
items.description: Chart the explosive rise of rock 'n' roll from Chuck Berry and Elvis to the British Invasion and psychedelic era of the 1960s.

items.title: Pop Culture: From Motown to Michael Jackson
items.description: Explore the rise of the pop music industry—from Motown's soul assembly line to disco, Michael Jackson's global stardom, and the MTV revolution.

items.title: World Music: When Cultures Meet and Mix
items.description: Survey the global richness of music—African rhythms, Latin salsa, Indian ragas, and K-pop—and how cultural exchange creates new musical forms.

items.title: Electronic Beats: Synthesizers, Techno, and Hip-Hop
items.description: Trace the rise of electronic music from Moog synthesizers and Kraftwerk to Detroit techno, and the birth of hip-hop in the Bronx.

items.title: Renaissance Music: Polyphony and the Birth of Harmony
items.description: Discover how Renaissance composers wove multiple voices together, invented the madrigal, and used the printing press to spread music.

items.title: Baroque Grandeur: Bach, Handel, and the Birth of Opera
items.description: Enter the age of counterpoint and basso continuo, where Bach perfected fugue and Handel moved audiences to tears with Messiah.

items.title: Classical Clarity: Haydn, Mozart, and the Perfection of Form
items.description: Discover how Classical composers perfected sonata form, the symphony, and the string quartet in an era of elegance and balance.

items.title: Beethoven: The Revolutionary at the Crossroads
items.description: Follow Beethoven through three compositional periods as he transformed Classical forms into vehicles of personal and universal drama.

items.title: The Romantic Century: Emotion, Color, and National Identity
items.description: Survey the 19th-century Romantic era, from Chopin's piano poetry to nationalist symphonic poems that gave voice to oppressed peoples.

items.title: The Fall of the Roman Republic: Why Caesar Crossed the Rubicon
items.description: The Roman Republic lasted 500 years before collapsing under civil war and dictatorship in the 1st century BCE. Caesar, Pompey, Brutus — the last act of the Republic.

items.title: Savings Strategy Complete Guide: Goal-Based Plans, Account Comparison, and Tax Advantages
items.description: Goal-matched savings strategies, comparing savings accounts vs. Roth IRA vs. 401(k) vs. brokerage accounts, maximizing tax advantages, emergency fund sizing, reaching \$100,000 simulations, and a step-by-step savings roadmap from your 20s through retirement.

items.title: Intro to the Giant Planets — How to Compare Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune
items.description: The outer giant planets of the solar system, split into gas giants and ice giants, explained through their atmospheres, rings, moons, and the missions that have explored them.

items.title: Intro to Gravity and Orbits — Understanding Planetary Motion by Imagining a Thrown Ball
items.description: An intro astronomy lecture that explains gravity, free fall, orbits, and escape velocity through the simple analogy of throwing a ball, paired with visual components.

items.title: Science Learning Hub — A Suggested Order for Studying the Solar System, Stars, Black Holes, the Brain, and Sleep
items.description: A science content hub for beginners, laying out a suggested reading order for the universe, life, the brain, sleep, and habits.

items.title: Intro to Light Speed and Light-Years — Understanding Cosmic Distance as a Sense of Time
items.description: An introductory science lecture that explains the speed of light, light-years, cosmic distances, and the time delay of starlight using everyday analogies and tables, accessible even to first-time learners.

items.title: Intro to Moon Phases, Eclipses, and Tides — Why the Moon Looks Different Every Day
items.description: A single explanation covering the phases of the crescent, first-quarter, full, and last-quarter moon, plus the principles behind solar eclipses, lunar eclipses, and the tides.

items.title: Intro to the Rocky Planets — Learning the Solar System by Comparing Mercury, Venus, Earth, and Mars
items.description: A beginner-friendly science lecture comparing the solar system's four inner rocky planets by distance, atmosphere, surface, and exploration history.

items.title: Intro to Seasons and Earth's Axial Tilt — Why Do Summer and Winter Happen?
items.description: Explains, with visuals and tables, that seasons are caused not by Earth's distance from the Sun but by the tilt of Earth's axis, the angle of sunlight, and day length.

items.title: Solar System, Stars, and Black Holes - A Beginner's Map of Space Science
items.description: A beginner-friendly lecture that connects planets, the Sun, stars, galaxies, and black holes through scale, gravity, and energy.

items.title: Intro to Sound and Waves — Understanding Frequency, Amplitude, and Wavelength Through Ripples and Guitar Strings
items.description: An introductory science lecture that makes sound, waves, amplitude, frequency, wavelength, resonance, and the Doppler effect easy to understand through water ripples and stringed-instrument analogies.

items.title: The Scientific Revolution: From Copernicus to Newton, How the World Was Overturned
items.description: From Copernicus's heliocentric theory in 1543 to Newton's Principia in 1687, 150 years transformed humanity's understanding of the cosmos — and how we know anything at all.

items.title: The Silk Road: The Ancient Internet That Connected East and West
items.description: The Silk Road was never a single road, and it wasn't just silk. It was the ancient world's information superhighway — carrying religion, technology, disease, and art alongside silk and spice.

items.title: Simulation Theory: Is Reality a Video Game?
items.description: Elon Musk believes there is a 'one in a billion' chance we are in base reality. Philosophers and physicists are starting to agree. Are we just NPCs in a cosmic server?

items.title: Sleep Architecture: Science of Dreams and Deep Rest
items.description: What happens in the brain while we sleep? Secrets of brain cleaning via the Glymphatic System and sleep cycles.

items.title: Sleep Chronotype Test: Are You a Morning Person or a Night Owl?
items.description: A test for identifying your sleep chronotype. Find out whether you're a Lion, Bear, Wolf, or Dolphin, and get an optimal sleep and work schedule matched to your biological rhythm.

items.title: The Science of Sleep: Evidence-Based Ways to Sleep Better
items.description: A complete guide to the neuroscience of sleep — sleep stages (REM and NREM), the effects of sleep deprivation, sleep hygiene, CBT-I for insomnia, and how to build the optimal sleep environment.

items.title: The Science of Sleep and Stress — A Routine Guide to How Your Body Actually Recovers
items.description: A science-based guide connecting sleep pressure, circadian rhythm, and the sympathetic/parasympathetic nervous system to help you design a stress-recovery routine.

items.title: The Complete Guide to Small Weddings by Country — Cost, Format, and Checklists
items.description: How small weddings look, cost, and get planned in Korea, Japan, the United States, and Europe — a country-by-country breakdown with a shared prep checklist.

items.title: Soccer Rules Explained — A 5-Minute Guide for Beginners
items.description: Everything from squad size and match time to offside, fouls, cards, and VAR — a beginner-friendly rundown of soccer's Laws of the Game as set by IFAB.

items.title: The Social Contract: Why We Obey
items.description: Man is born free, and everywhere he is in chains.' Why do we agree to follow laws, pay taxes, and let the government punish us? We signed a contract we never saw.

items.title: The Life and Death of Stars, and Supernovae — From Nuclear Fusion to Neutron Stars and Black Holes
items.description: Explains how a star is born, shines, and dies by connecting mass, nuclear fusion, supernovae, white dwarfs, neutron stars, and black holes.

items.title: Stock Basics — How to Read Charts — Candlesticks, Moving Averages & Support/Resistance Explained
items.description: A technical analysis primer for beginners who find stock charts intimidating. Learn the anatomy of candlesticks, what moving averages reveal, golden crosses, death crosses, and the basics of support and resistance lines.

items.title: Stoic Philosophy and Anger: Seneca on Becoming the Master of Your Emotions
items.description: Seneca called anger the one emotion that turns human beings into beasts. Two thousand years on, Stoic philosophy's sharpest insights on rage remain entirely practical for modern emotional life.

items.title: Marcus Aurelius and Resilience: How to Protect Yourself in a Shaking World
items.description: Through the 'Meditations' of Marcus Aurelius, a Roman emperor and philosopher, learn the wisdom of Stoic philosophy to manage modern anxiety and cultivate inner strength.

items.title: Stoicism: How to Find Peace Amidst Digital Noise
items.description: The world is becoming increasingly chaotic and shakes us. We learn the wisdom of distinguishing between 'what can be controlled' and 'what cannot,' taught by Stoic philosophers 2,000 years ago.

items.title: Stoicism: Remember Death (Memento Mori) and Love Your Fate (Amor Fati)
items.description: A sophisticated technique for maintaining unshakeable peace when the world doesn't go your way. We provide a modern reinterpretation of the core wisdom of Stoicism from Marcus Aurelius and Seneca.

items.title: Stoicism, Fully Explained: Marcus Aurelius's Wisdom for Modern Life
items.description: A complete guide to the core principles of Stoicism and how to apply them to modern life — the wisdom of Marcus Aurelius, Epictetus, and Seneca, with everyday practices.

items.title: Stoicism: An Operating System for Chaos
items.description: It was not just Marcus Aurelius. It was a slave (Epictetus) and a shipwreck survivor (Zeno). Stoicism is not about suppressing emotion; it is about domestication of perception.

items.title: String Theory and Parallel Universes: The Tiniest Threads of Existence and the Grand Multiverse
items.description: What if the universe is made not of points, but of vibrations of tiny 'strings'? We explore modern physics' boldest challenges: unseen dimensions and infinite parallel universes.

items.title: Sufism: The Path of Radical Love
items.description: Rumi is the most quoted poet in the world, but he was not just a romantic. He was a Sufi mystic. Sufism teaches that the Beloved is not a person, but God disguised as everything.

items.title: Sympathetic vs Parasympathetic Nervous System: How Your Body Responds to Stress
items.description: Complete guide to your autonomic nervous system — sympathetic vs parasympathetic, how to activate each, and daily routines to restore balance for better sleep, focus, and stress resilience.

items.title: Table Tennis Rules Explained — 11-Point Games and the Serve
items.description: 11-point games, alternating serves every 2 points, serve rules (the toss, the open serve), and doubles order — a beginner-friendly rundown of table tennis based on ITTF rules.

items.title: Wu Wei: The Art of Effortless Action
items.description: In a hustle culture that worships 'The Grind,' Taoism offers a radical alternative: Do nothing, and leave nothing undone. This is the philosophy of Flow.

items.title: Wu Wei: How to Accomplish by Not Striving
items.description: Are you suffering because the world doesn't go according to your will? Through the wisdom of 'Wu Wei' (natural non-action) from Lao Tzu's Tao Te Ching, we learn how to win by entrusting ourselves t...

items.title: Taxes in South Korea, Part 1: Capital Gains, Inheritance, and Gifts
items.description: An introduction to South Korean taxes on asset transfers, inheritance, and gifts. Korean examples do not describe tax rules in other countries.

items.title: Taxes in South Korea, Part 2: Property, Income, Corporate Tax, and VAT
items.description: An introduction to South Korean property, income, corporate, and value-added taxes. Korean examples do not describe tax rules in other countries.

items.title: Techno-Animism: Do Androids Have Spirits?
items.description: Why do Japanese and Korean people thank their cleaning robots? Why does the West fear AI while the East embraces it? The answer lies in Animism.

items.title: Tennis Rules Explained — How Scoring Works, From Zero
items.description: The 15-30-40 scoring system, games, sets, and matches, serving and faults, deuce and tiebreaks — a beginner-friendly rundown of tennis rules based on ITF regulations.

items.title: Testing Activities: Enjoy It Like a Game, Not an Exam
items.description: From Two Truths and One Lie to Kahoot, explore 7 testing activities that use gamification to verify knowledge and maximize metacognitive review efficiency.

items.title: A Single Flower Cannot Make a Forest: Why Together is the Last Bastion of Our Souls
items.description: Exploring why the value of togetherness is the ultimate remedy for our souls in an era of isolation and spiritual disconnection.

items.title: Korea Legal Interest Calculator: Civil, Commercial & Litigation Rate
items.description: Enter principal, period, and interest type (Civil 5% / Commercial 6% / Litigation special rate 12%) to instantly calculate statutory interest and total principal-plus-interest. Useful for loans, damages, and unpaid wages.

items.title: The Radiant Counterattack of Useless Things: How Hobbies Lead Our Lives into the Deep Sea
items.description: Beyond the age of efficiency, discover how the 'uselessness' of hobbies provides depth, resilience, and a three-dimensional richness to our existence.

items.title: Utilitarianism: The Math of Morality
items.description: Would you kill one person to save five? Utilitarianism says 'Yes.' It sounds logical, but it leads to terrifying conclusions. This is the main algorithm of AI ethics.

items.title: The Vagus Nerve: The Biological Highway of Calm
items.description: The Vagus Nerve is the 'King of the Parasympathetic System.' Learn how this massive neural superhighway controls your stress response and how to 'tune' it for ultimate resilience.

items.title: The Vikings: Raiders, Traders, Explorers — and America's First Visitors
items.description: The Vikings terrorized medieval Europe — but they were also the first Europeans in North America, the founders of Russia, and traders who reached Baghdad. The real story.

items.title: Volleyball Rules Explained — Rally Scoring and Rotation in One Guide
items.description: From players, sets, and rally scoring to the 3-touch rule, rotation, the libero, and positions — a beginner-friendly rundown of volleyball based on FIVB rules.

items.title: Wabi-Sabi: The Ultimate Aesthetic Discovered in Imperfection
items.description: Breaking free from the obsession with perfection and learning to love the depth of time embedded in old and scratched things. We rediscover the value of transience and simplicity through 'Wabi-Sabi...

items.title: Wedding Etiquette Around the World — Gifts, Dress, and Guest Manners
items.description: A detailed, country-by-country guide to wedding guest etiquette in Korea, Japan, China, the US, Europe, and India — covering gift money, dress, and taboos to avoid.

items.title: Writing from Memory Activities: Retrieval Practice for Long-term Memory
items.description: Boost metacognition and solidify long-term memory with these 9 effective writing activities, featuring everything from memory brainwriting to digital word clouds.

items.title: The Complete Tax Refund Guide: Deductions, Credits, and How to Maximize Your Return
items.description: Your employer withholds income tax throughout the year based on an estimate — but your actual tax liability may be lower. This guide covers how withholding works, the most valuable deductions and credits available to US wage earners, key IRS deadlines, and how to avoid the most common filing mistakes.

items.title: Zero’s Paradox: How Non-Nutritive Sweeteners Affect Metabolic Health
items.description: Are zero calorie drinks really ‘zero’? We analyze the molecular biological mechanisms of artificial sweeteners, their effects on the gut microbiota, and the brain's insulin response.

items.title: Cap.1 Introducción a la Contabilidad — Lo que debes saber antes de leer un balance
items.description: La definición y el propósito de la contabilidad, contabilidad financiera vs contabilidad de gestión, el principio de la partida doble y las hipótesis contables fundamentales — primera clase de la serie Contabilidad Básica.

items.title: Cap.2 Balance y Cuenta de Resultados — Estructura de los estados financieros
items.description: Análisis detallado de la estructura del balance de situación y la cuenta de pérdidas y ganancias. Aprende a leer los dos estados financieros más importantes y a entender la clasificación de activos y pasivos corrientes y no corrientes.

items.title: Cap.3 Estado de Flujos de Efectivo — Por qué beneficio ≠ tesorería
items.description: Las tres categorías de actividades del estado de flujos de efectivo, método directo vs método indirecto, y por qué una empresa rentable puede quedarse sin liquidez — el estado financiero más ignorado pero frecuentemente más revelador.

items.title: Economía del comportamiento — Dónde falla el modelo estándar
items.description: Traza el mapa del curso: qué supuestos del modelo económico estándar revisa la economía del comportamiento (preferencias, creencias, proceso de decisión), la racionalidad limitada, el papel de la evidencia de laboratorio y de campo y el problema de la replicabilidad.

items.title: Economía del comportamiento — Replicabilidad, economía del bienestar conductual y límites de la política
items.description: Cierra el curso distinguiendo los hallazgos debilitados por grandes replicaciones (como el agotamiento del ego) de los sólidos, preguntándose qué criterio usar cuando elección y bienestar divergen, y tratando los impuestos correctores sobre internalidades y la explotación de sesgos por las empresas.

items.title: Economía del comportamiento — Teoría prospectiva I: punto de referencia y aversión a las pérdidas
items.description: Presenta con fórmulas y un gráfico la función de valor de la teoría prospectiva, en la que la utilidad depende de ganancias y pérdidas respecto a un punto de referencia y no del nivel de riqueza, y explica con ejemplos numéricos el coeficiente de aversión a las pérdidas, el efecto reflejo y los efectos marco.

items.title: Economía del comportamiento — Teoría prospectiva II: ponderación de probabilidades y efecto dotación
items.description: Explica con la teoría prospectiva la función de ponderación que sobrepondera las probabilidades pequeñas e infrapondera las grandes, la paradoja de Allais, el patrón cuádruple de actitudes ante el riesgo, el efecto dotación y el sesgo del statu quo, y valora la solidez de la evidencia.

items.title: Economía del comportamiento — Sesgo del presente e inconsistencia temporal
items.description: Muestra con cifras la diferencia entre el descuento exponencial y el cuasihiperbólico (β-δ) y por qué se invierten las preferencias, y presenta la diferencia entre agentes ingenuos y sofisticados, los mecanismos de compromiso y diseños como Save More Tomorrow.

items.title: Economía del comportamiento — Heurísticos de juicio y creencias sesgadas
items.description: Muestra con ejemplos numéricos cómo los heurísticos de representatividad, disponibilidad y anclaje y ajuste se apartan sistemáticamente de la actualización bayesiana: desatención a la tasa base, falacia de la conjunción, falacia del jugador, exceso de confianza y sesgo de confirmación.

items.title: Economía del comportamiento — Contabilidad mental y costes hundidos
items.description: Enlaza con la teoría prospectiva, con ejemplos numéricos, la contabilidad mental que rompe el supuesto de que el dinero es fungible, la utilidad de la transacción y los precios de referencia, la separación e integración de ganancias y pérdidas, el efecto de los costes hundidos y los objetivos de ingresos.

items.title: Economía del comportamiento — Preferencias sociales: equidad, reciprocidad y confianza
items.description: Resume los resultados experimentales de los juegos del ultimátum, del dictador, de bienes públicos y de confianza, calcula los umbrales de rechazo con el modelo de aversión a la desigualdad de Fehr y Schmidt, y trata la reciprocidad, el intercambio de regalos y la expulsión de la motivación por los incentivos monetarios.

items.title: Economía del comportamiento — Finanzas conductuales: límites al arbitraje y sesgos de los inversores
items.description: Explica por qué el arbitraje no corrige los precios aunque haya inversores sesgados (límites al arbitraje), presenta la evidencia de campo sobre el efecto disposición y el exceso de operaciones, y el enigma de la prima de riesgo visto desde la aversión miope a las pérdidas.
tags: enigma de la prima de riesgo

items.title: Economía del comportamiento — Arquitectura de la elección y nudges
items.description: Presenta la evidencia de que las opciones por defecto, las normas sociales y la forma de presentar la información cambian las elecciones (adscripción automática a pensiones, informes de energía), las pruebas a gran escala del tamaño de los nudges y el paternalismo libertario y sus críticas.

items.title: Introducción a la economía — Escasez, coste de oportunidad y sistemas económicos
items.description: Repasa cómo calcular el coste de oportunidad como relación marginal de transformación y distinguirlo de los costes hundidos, y qué dice de forma distinta la FPP sobre la eficiencia, el crecimiento y los costes crecientes.

items.title: Introducción a la economía — Oferta y demanda: cómo se forman los precios de mercado
items.description: Repasa la diferencia entre la variación de la cantidad demandada y el desplazamiento de la demanda, cómo calcular la variación del ingreso total con la elasticidad-precio y por qué un precio máximo crea escasez.

items.title: Introducción a la economía — Teoría del consumidor: utilidad, curvas de indiferencia y restricción presupuestaria
items.description: Deduce por qué la RMS iguala el precio relativo en una solución interior y repasa dónde falla esa condición: soluciones de esquina, bienes Giffen y efectos renta y sustitución.

items.title: Introducción a la economía — Teoría del productor: estructura de costes y maximización del beneficio
items.description: Encuentra el punto de cierre a partir de la relación entre el coste marginal y el coste medio a corto plazo, y calcula por qué IMg = CMg maximiza el beneficio y por qué los costes fijos no entran en esa condición.

items.title: Introducción a la economía — Estructuras de mercado: competencia perfecta, monopolio y oligopolio
items.description: Compara las cantidades y precios de competencia y monopolio con IMg = CMg para calcular la pérdida irrecuperable, y repasa el incentivo que rompe la colusión en el oligopolio.

items.title: Introducción a la economía — Fallos del mercado e intervención pública: externalidades, bienes públicos e información asimétrica
items.description: Cuantifica la brecha entre costes privados y sociales de una externalidad y repasa las condiciones en que el mecanismo de precios deja de funcionar con los bienes públicos y el mercado de «cacharros».

items.title: Hacienda pública — Fallos del mercado y papel del Estado
items.description: Partiendo de los dos teoremas del bienestar, este capítulo presenta con ejemplos numéricos la condición de Samuelson para los bienes públicos, el impuesto pigouviano y el teorema de Coase para las externalidades y los fallos del Estado: cuándo está justificada la intervención pública y cuándo fracasa.

items.title: Síntesis de hacienda pública — Usar todas las herramientas con un impuesto sobre el carbono
items.description: Sigue una sola política, el impuesto sobre el carbono, a través de externalidades, incidencia, exceso de gravamen, uso de la recaudación, distribución y análisis coste-beneficio para enlazar las herramientas de los capítulos 1 a 9, y resume las fórmulas clave en una tabla.

items.title: Hacienda pública — Incidencia fiscal y exceso de gravamen
items.description: Quién ingresa un impuesto y quién lo soporta son cosas distintas. Este capítulo reparte la incidencia según las elasticidades, mide el exceso de gravamen con el triángulo de Harberger y presenta la regla de Ramsey y los criterios de equidad fiscal, con ejemplos numéricos.

items.title: Hacienda pública — Gasto público: redistribución, prestaciones en especie y elección pública
items.description: Presenta la diferencia entre transferencias en dinero y en especie, el tipo marginal del 100 % que crean las prestaciones complementarias, el diseño por tramos del crédito fiscal por rentas del trabajo, el teorema del votante mediano y la búsqueda de rentas: cómo se decide el gasto público y qué cambia.

items.title: Hacienda pública — Impuesto sobre la renta y sobre sociedades: efectos sobre el trabajo, el ahorro y la inversión
items.description: Presenta con ejemplos numéricos los efectos sustitución y renta del impuesto sobre la oferta de trabajo, la elasticidad de la renta imponible y el tipo que maximiza la recaudación, la tributación de los intereses y el ahorro, y el sesgo a favor de la deuda y la doble imposición del impuesto sobre sociedades.

items.title: Hacienda pública — IVA e impuestos indirectos
items.description: Explica con ejemplos numéricos por qué el IVA, recaudado en cada fase, solo pesa sobre el consumo final, la diferencia entre tipo cero y exención, el debate sobre la regresividad, las reglas de Ramsey, Corlett-Hague y Atkinson-Stiglitz y los impuestos correctores.

items.title: Hacienda pública — Política fiscal: multiplicadores, equivalencia ricardiana y dinámica de la deuda
items.description: Presenta con ejemplos numéricos los multiplicadores del gasto, de los impuestos y del presupuesto equilibrado, cómo los estabilizadores automáticos reducen el multiplicador, las condiciones de la equivalencia ricardiana, la dinámica de la ratio de deuda (r−g)b y las reglas fiscales.

items.title: Hacienda pública — Haciendas locales y federalismo fiscal
items.description: Presenta qué servicios públicos deben prestar el Gobierno central y los locales (teorema de descentralización de Oates), el voto con los pies (hipótesis de Tiebout), los efectos renta y precio de las transferencias incondicionales y condicionadas, el efecto papel matamoscas y la restricción presupuestaria blanda.

items.title: Hacienda pública — Economía de las pensiones públicas y del seguro de salud
items.description: Presenta con ejemplos numéricos por qué hace falta el seguro social (selección adversa, riesgo moral, miopía), el rendimiento n+g de las pensiones de reparto y la condición de Aaron, la tasa de dependencia y el tipo de cotización, la espiral de selección adversa en salud, el copago y el pago a proveedores.

items.title: Hacienda pública — Sistemas presupuestarios y análisis coste-beneficio
items.description: Presenta con ejemplos numéricos las diferencias entre presupuesto por partidas, por resultados, PPBS y base cero, el incrementalismo, y el valor actual neto, la tasa social de descuento, los precios sombra y el valor estadístico de la vida del análisis coste-beneficio.

items.title: Jesa: Los muertos no se han ido
items.description: En Occidente, se visita una tumba una vez al año. En Corea, los antepasados vienen a cenar. Jesa no es solo 'adoración'; es una relación continua con los muertos.

items.title: La Peste Negra: Cómo una plaga salvó a Europa
items.description: La peste bubónica mató al 50% de Europa. Fue apocalípticamente trágico. Pero también terminó con el feudalismo y dio a luz a la clase media. El desastre crea apalancamiento.

items.title: Sunyata: La sabiduría del vacío
items.description: ¿Está el vacío vacío o está lleno? El concepto budista de Sunyata (Vacuidad) no es nihilismo. Es la comprensión de que todo está conectado porque nada existe solo.

items.title: Confucianismo: La geometría de las relaciones humanas
items.description: No es una religión; es un sistema operativo social. Durante 2000 años, el confucianismo ha definido las jerarquías de Asia Oriental. ¿Es una reliquia opresiva o el secreto de la armonía social?

items.title: El Problema Difícil: ¿Quién conduce?
items.description: Sabemos cómo se activan las neuronas. Sabemos cómo el cerebro procesa la luz. Pero NO tenemos idea de cómo esa carne se convierte en 'la sensación de ver rojo'. Este es el Problema Difícil de la Co...

items.title: Guía completa del pensamiento crítico: Falacias lógicas y cómo juzgar mejor
items.description: Una guía completa sobre los principios fundamentales del pensamiento crítico (Critical Thinking), 20 falacias lógicas, métodos de evaluación de evidencias y el método socrático. La guía definitiva para tomar mejores decisiones y debatir con rigor.

items.title: Microeconomía — Escasez, coste de oportunidad y frontera de posibilidades de producción
items.description: Calcula el coste de oportunidad como suma de costes explícitos e implícitos, explica por qué crece la relación marginal de transformación a lo largo de la FPP, distingue eficiencia técnica y asignativa y muestra cómo tratar los costes hundidos, con números y un gráfico.

items.title: Microeconomía — Fallos de mercado: externalidades, bienes públicos e información
items.description: Calcula las externalidades como la diferencia entre coste marginal privado y social, compara el impuesto pigouviano, el teorema de Coase y los impuestos frente a los límites de cantidad (Weitzman), y presenta el polizón en los bienes públicos, la selección adversa en el mercado de «cacharros» y la señalización.

items.title: Macroeconomía — Medición de la renta nacional y sus identidades
items.description: Comprueba con los números de una economía por qué el PIB medido por la producción, el gasto y la renta es el mismo, y presenta el PIB nominal y real, el deflactor, el PIB frente a la RNB, la identidad ahorro–inversión y por qué el PIB no es una medida de bienestar.

items.title: Macroeconomía — Medición de la inflación y el desempleo
items.description: Presenta con números cómo se construye el índice de precios de consumo y sus sesgos, la diferencia entre IPC y deflactor del PIB, la ecuación de Fisher y la redistribución que causa la inflación imprevista, los denominadores de las tasas de paro, empleo y actividad y los trabajadores desanimados, y los tres tipos de desempleo.

items.title: Macroeconomía — Demanda y oferta de dinero, y filtraciones del multiplicador
items.description: Presenta las funciones del dinero y los agregados monetarios, calcula el multiplicador monetario a partir de la base monetaria con el coeficiente de efectivo, el coeficiente de reservas y las reservas excedentarias, explica por qué la base monetaria se vuelve endógena con un objetivo de tipos de interés y trata la relación precio de los bonos–tipos y la teoría cuantitativa del dinero.

items.title: Macroeconomía — Fundamentos del modelo IS-LM
items.description: Deriva el equilibrio del mercado de bienes IS y el del mercado de dinero LM en un modelo lineal, y compara con los mismos números y un gráfico el efecto expulsión de un aumento del gasto público y la transmisión de una expansión monetaria.

items.title: Macroeconomía — La función de consumo: de Keynes a la renta permanente
items.description: Calcula el multiplicador con la función de consumo keynesiana y la cruz keynesiana y, partiendo del enigma de Kuznets, presenta las hipótesis de la renta permanente y del ciclo vital, el consumo como paseo aleatorio y por qué las restricciones de liquidez cambian la propensión marginal a consumir, con números y un gráfico.

items.title: Macroeconomía — La función de inversión: el coste de uso del capital
